sections.title: Queer Media Technologies
sections.description: For decades, queer individuals have created, tinkered, and transformed media technologies to build collective movements and survive in a world that doesn’t want them. This course explores those moments and sites at which queer subjects have shaped or been shaped by the development of media technologies in the late 20th and early 21st centuries. Assigned readings, projects, and media will also address the shifting cultural constructions of queerness as it intersects with other dimensions of social identity and difference. Queerness offers the potential for thinking possibility, sideways, and otherwise to normativity, convention, and socially sanctioned reality. By critically investigating the intersection of queer studies with media studies, we will understand the ways in which queer theory provides us with tools for engaging and remaking our contemporary media landscape.
